study.title: Mark 14 The Passion of Jesus, the Suit and the Fall of Peter
study.overview: Mark 14 presents the final line of Jesus" earthly ministry with a strong contrast between fidelity and betrayal. The religious leaders plan to kill him, a woman honors him with an expensive and prophetic act, Judas hand over, Jesus institutes the Paschal supper as a sign of his saving death, and the disciples fail to watch and remain unstable. In the garden, Jesus submits to the Father in real anguish; then he is imprisoned, judged with false and condemned testimonies. The chapter ends with the denial of Peter and his bitter crying, showing that the word of Jesus is fulfilled and that human frailty is exposed before the cross.

outline.title: Conspiracy, anointing in Bethany and betrayal of Judas
outline.explanation: The chief priests and scribes seek to arrest Jesus by mistake, but they fear the people. In Bethany, a woman pours expensive perfume on Jesus, and he interprets his gesture as preparation for the grave. Then Judas goes to the religious leaders to deliver him, initiating treason for money.

outline.title: Preparation of Easter, supper, new alliance and announcement of denials
outline.explanation: Jesus directs the preparation of Easter with sovereign knowledge of events. At the table, he proclaims the betrayal of one of the twelve, and institutes the bread and cup as signs of his body and blood shed by many, connected to the kingdom of God. Then it foresees the dispersion of the disciples and the denial of Peter, even before his excessive confidence.

outline.title: Gethsemane: prayer, submission and vigilance
outline.explanation: In the garden, Jesus enters into deep anguish and asks that, if possible, the cup pass from him, but submits to the will of the Father. Meanwhile, the disciples slept repeatedly, and Jesus calls them to watch and pray not to enter into temptation. The hour of surrender approaches and Judas comes to meet him.

outline.title: Prison, trial, abandonment and denial of Peter
outline.explanation: Jesus is imprisoned by an armed crowd sent by the leaders. All the disciples flee. Faced with the counsel, false and contradictory testimonies arise; Jesus confesses to be the Christ and speaks of the Son of man exalted at the right hand of the Mighty, which leads to condemnation for blasphemy. Meanwhile, Peter denies him three times and weeps as he remembers the word of Jesus.

study.context: The chapter takes place in the final phase of Jesus" presence in Jerusalem, near the Passover and the unleavened bread, a Jewish feast mentioned in the text itself. The notes provided identify Bethany as the place of the anointing and show that supper occurs in the paschal context. It is also evident that the conflict intensifies between Jesus and the religious leaders of Jerusalem, culminating in his judgment by the high priest and the council.
study.theology: Mark 14 highlights Jesus" sovereignty over the events of passion: he is not surprised, but he walks to the cross in obedience to God's plan. The anointing in Bethany anticipates its burial and shows that true love perceives, albeit partially, the meaning of the imminent death of Christ. The supper reveals that his death is substitutive and pactual: his blood is shed by many and inaugurates the new covenant. The chapter also exposes the weakness of the disciples: Peter's self-confidence, the sleep in the hour of watch, the general escape and the final denial. In contrast, Jesus remains faithful, submissive to the Father and trusting in the Scriptures. Suffering is not only physical or social; there is deep anguish in the soul of Jesus, but without rebellion against the divine will. Finally, Jesus' confession before the court affirms his Messianic identity and his future exaltation, even when the world rejects him.

scholarViews.insight: The cup represents the blood of Jesus shed as sacrifice and as the beginning of God's covenant with his people; the term "many" points to a wide range.
The Paschal supper does not prevent Jesus from facing the pain; on the contrary, he prepares for sufferings remaining turned to God and to the solemnity of the moment.
The expression "Aba," Paio expresses filial tenderness and full submission of Jesus to the will of the Father, uniting reverence and trust.

questions: What does Jesus" reaction to the woman's offering in Bethany teaches about sacrificial adoration and spiritual discernment?
In what respects the Lord's supper in this chapter points to the death of Jesus as a covenant and sacrifice for many?
In what ways does Peter's self-confidence and the absent vigilance of the other disciples look like our own weaknesses before temptation?
study.practice: Read the chapter as called to concrete fidelity: value Jesus above cost, watch and pray when pressure increases, and does not trust emotional strength or impulsive promises. Also learn from Peter what restoration begins when the word of Christ is remembered and the heart is broken. In practice, set aside time for obedient prayer, examine his motivations in serving, and approach the Lord's table with gratitude for the death of Christ and reverently for the new covenant he has sealed.
study.uncertainty: The study is limited to the notes provided and the text of Mark 14. It is not possible to affirm with certainty additional historical details, nor to fully harmonize differences with other Gospels without leaving the sources given. The expressions of Jesus" supper, covenant, and identity are interpreted here in Protestant evangelical key, but theological readings of the text remain, not unavoidable confessional impositions.
